description: Explicit exceptions and product decisions for repository-discovered frontend surface families. Discovery remains fail-closed; absence of a matching rule blocks dispatch.

rules.rationale: The dependency-light public platform shell and browser-safe catalog are the governed entrypoint for the unified frontend.
The host-scoped root handler returns public discovery metadata for every registered method and is consumed as API bootstrap data, not as a standalone product surface.
Existing Connect assets remain a compatibility surface while the unified shell is introduced.
Existing Local Manager browser pages remain supported until wave F4 reaches verified parity.
Health contracts feed status components but are not standalone navigation destinations.
Status contracts feed operational views but are not standalone navigation destinations.
The overlay exposes JWT-scoped Activation session context and safe session metadata as OAuth API responses consumed by the Tenant Activation GPT; it does not render a standalone browser surface.
Session reference, turn, and closure handlers are authenticated archive APIs consumed by governed GPT and Activation clients; they are not independent navigation or embedded UI surfaces.

auth_rules.rationale: The webhook verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 against the preserved raw request body before ingestion. This policy exposes that inline HMAC guarantee to route inventory without changing runtime behavior.
The root discovery handler has no authentication middleware and returns only host-scoped route metadata for every Express router.all method.
The legacy status root handler is mounted without authentication and returns public service metadata.
Deployment identity, version, and aggregate health are intentionally unauthenticated readiness metadata and return no credentials.
The version, checksum manifest, and allowlisted agent release files are public bootstrap artifacts; credential-bearing installers use separate signed links.
Each download verifies a short-lived signed or hashed token from the token query parameter before returning credential-bearing or private artifacts.
Heartbeat resolution accepts the backend bearer value or the registered connector secret/local API key and rejects requests without a bearer token.
These browser shell, bootstrap, and navigation documents are public entrypoints; their data calls enforce user or device authentication separately.
Pairing initiation is public by design; preview and polling require the short-lived device code and polling secret defined in their request contracts.
The imported service handlers validate either the signed-in Local Manager user JWT or a scoped Local Manager device bearer before accessing linked-device state.
These transport-level public endpoints validate a short-lived, single-use capability token embedded in the path before reading or consuming an intake session.
The Connect policy document is public browser bootstrap metadata and contains no credentials or tenant records.
OAuth authorization-server and protected-resource discovery documents must be reachable before a bearer token exists and expose only standards-based endpoint, scope, and resource metadata.
Identity initiation and credential exchange must be reachable before a platform bearer exists; each operation validates its OAuth, password, reset-token, or client-credential inputs.

The SSO revocation endpoint is intentionally reachable without a bearer middleware because it accepts the current SSO cookie or a submitted session token, validates it server-side, clears the cookie, and returns an idempotent secret-free result.
The status page and incident summary are deliberately public operational transparency surfaces.
The deterministic smoke-provider registry and fixtures are intentionally public, non-secret demo data used by the platform shell.

The published Act-as-User Custom GPT contract exposes exactly one backendApiKeyAuth scheme. The runtime middleware retains its bounded compatibility parser for bearer-form backend credentials and user JWTs, but those alternatives are not published as Custom GPT security schemes; the route remains fail-closed and additionally requires the privileged Act-as-User principal guard.

Runtime database binding and Hostinger bootstrap dry-run evidence are service-only operational endpoints. The generic backend guard keeps compatibility parsing for user JWTs, but these routes explicitly reject non-service auth modes before reading runtime binding or invoking bootstrap logic.
